items.bewering: Die Egiptenare het geglo dat 'n farao na sy dood verder leef.
items.bron: Iziko Museums of South Africa, 'Egypt in South Africa: burial customs' (egyptinsouthafrica.iziko.org.za/burial_customs/): the soul or ka stayed with the mummy so the dead would continue to 'live' in the afterlife; the pharaoh was buried with what he would need there.

items.bewering: Daarom het hulle vir baie farao's 'n reusagtige graf van groot klipblokke gebou. So 'n graf word 'n piramide genoem
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Egyptian pyramids': at least 118-138 pyramids identified in Egypt, most of them tombs for pharaohs and their consorts; Old Kingdom pyramids were mainly stone. 'Baie' (not 'alle') is correct: pharaohs of the New Kingdom were not buried in pyramids, and Middle Kingdom pyramids were mainly mudbrick, but the Old Kingdom stone pyramids alone cover many pharaohs.

items.bewering: party ander belangrike mense het ook een gekry.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Giza pyramid complex': three queens' pyramids beside Khufu's and three subsidiary pyramids beside Menkaure's; Wikipedia, 'Egyptian pyramids': some pyramids were built for queens, e.g. the wife of Teti.

items.bewering: Die bouers moes elke kant en elke hoek noukeurig meet.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Pyramid of Giza': the four base sides differ in length by an average of only 58 mm, the base corners are square to a mean error of 12 seconds of arc, and the sides are aligned to the cardinal directions to within about a tenth of a degree.

items.bewering: Duisende werkers het jare lank saam aan 'n groot piramide gewerk.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Pyramid of Giza': built over about 26 years, average workforce about 13 200 with a peak of about 40 000 (1999 construction-management study); Mark Lehner's estimate of 20 000-30 000 at peak, reported in IEEE Spectrum and History.com. 'Duisende' and 'jare lank' sit safely inside every modern estimate.

items.bewering: By Giza staan drie bekende piramides naby mekaar.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Giza pyramid complex': three main pyramids, of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, all Fourth Dynasty. Smaller queens' pyramids also stand there; 'drie bekende' correctly leaves them out without denying them.

items.bewering: Die Groot Piramide is al meer as 4 500 jaar oud.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Pyramid of Giza': built c. 2600 BC; Ramsey et al. (2010) radiocarbon range 2613-2577 BC; conventional reign of Khufu c. 2589-2566 BC. That makes it about 4 590-4 640 years old in 2026, so 'meer as 4 500' holds on every chronology.

items.bewering: Die Groot Piramide
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Giza pyramid complex' and 'Great Pyramid of Giza': 'Great Pyramid' is the established name of Khufu's pyramid, the largest of the three. The lesson uses it as a name and makes no further superlative claim. No other superlative (eerste, oudste, grootste, enigste) occurs anywhere in the lesson.

items.bewering: Die ander twee is dié van Chafra (in Engels: Khafre) en Menkaoere (in Engels: Menkaure).
items.bron: Afrikaans Wikipedia, 'Piramides van Giza': 'Piramide van Chafra' and 'Piramide van Menkaoere'; English Wikipedia, 'Giza pyramid complex': Pyramid of Khafre (Khufu's son) and Pyramid of Menkaure (Khafre's son). Both spellings match their sources.

items.bewering: Die Groot Sfinks is 'n reusagtige beeld met 'n leeu se liggaam en 'n mens se kop.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Sphinx of Giza': a limestone statue of a reclining sphinx with a human head and a lion's body, about 73 m long and 20 m high.

items.bewering: Bouers het dit naby die piramides uit die kalksteen van die plek self gekap.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Sphinx of Giza': carved from the limestone bedrock of the Giza Plateau (a monolith), beside the causeway of Khafre's pyramid complex. AERA (Mark Lehner), 'Who built the Sphinx?': quarrymen cut the ditch around it and left a block of limestone from which it was carved.

items.bewering: Dit was moontlik 'n beskermer van die piramides.
items.bron: History.com, 'The Sphinx': in ancient Egypt the sphinx was a spiritual guardian, commonly placed in tomb and temple complexes; History Skills, 'The Great Sphinx': exact purpose still debated, but thought to have been a guardian figure over the Giza necropolis. Wikipedia, 'Great Sphinx of Giza' says the original purpose is not established. The lesson's 'moontlik' matches that state of knowledge exactly; it should not be firmed up.

items.bewering: Tempels was geboue waar die Egiptenare hulle gode vereer het.
items.bron: Egypt Exploration Society, 'Temples in Ancient Egypt' (ees.ac.uk): 'A temple was a house for the one or more deities it was dedicated to', with daily cult and offerings.

items.bewering: Hulle het geglo dat 'n god self in sy tempel woon.
items.bron: Egypt Exploration Society, 'Temples in Ancient Egypt': 'Gods were believed to live within their statues in the temple's shrine.' The heading's picture of a temple as a house for the gods is the Egyptians' own (the Egyptian word for temple meant 'god's house'), so the mapping holds: a learner reasoning from it to 'the god lives there and is looked after there' reaches what Egyptians believed.

items.bewering: Priesters het elke dag daar rituele vir die god uitgevoer.
items.bron: Egypt Exploration Society, 'Temples in Ancient Egypt': each temple had a daily ritual in which the high priest, acting for the pharaoh, opened the shrine each morning, greeted, dressed and fed the god's statue.

items.bewering: Die piramides, die Sfinks en baie tempels staan vandag nog.
items.blok: Ons kan dit vandag nog sien
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Giza pyramid complex': the three pyramids and the Sphinx stand on the Giza plateau today, part of the 'Memphis and its Necropolis' World Heritage Site (1979); Egypt Exploration Society, 'Temples in Ancient Egypt': surviving temples at Dendera, Edfu, Esna and Karnak.

items.bewering: Mense van regoor die wêreld kom kyk na hierdie erfenis.
items.blok: Ons kan dit vandag nog sien
items.bron: Egypt's Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, reported by Business Today Egypt and Scene Now: about 15 million international arrivals in the first nine months of 2025; the Giza pyramids topped site ticket sales, with Karnak second (Ahram Online). The site is on UNESCO's World Heritage List (Wikipedia, 'Giza pyramid complex').

items.bewering: Die klipgeboue is ook bewyse van hoe goed die Egiptenare kon beplan en bou.
items.blok: Ons kan dit vandag nog sien
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Great Pyramid of Giza': base sides equal to within 58 mm on average, corners square to within 12 arc-seconds, and a workforce organised over decades. The evidence supports the interpretation.

items.bewering: piramide: 'n Reusagtige graf van klipblokke, gebou vir 'n farao of ander belangrike mens.
items.bron: A glossary entry is read on its own, and on its own this one defines the word itself. But 'piramide' first names a shape: Grade 5 learners sort and name pyramids as 3-D objects in CAPS Mathematics (Intermediate Phase Mathematics CAPS, 3-D objects: prisms, cubes, cylinders, cones and pyramids). Pyramids elsewhere were not tombs: Mesoamerican pyramids were mainly temple platforms (History.com, 'Pyramids in Latin America'). Even in Egypt not all were of stone blocks: Middle Kingdom pyramids were mainly mudbrick (Wikipedia, 'Egyptian pyramids'). The entry is true of the Old Kingdom pyramids the lesson teaches, and false as a definition of the word.
items.regstelling: Tie the entry to ancient Egypt instead of defining the word as such, so it says that in ancient Egypt a pyramid was a huge tomb, usually of stone blocks, built for a pharaoh or another important person. A shape clause (square base, four sloping sides that meet at a point) would also make it true on its own. Do not change the study text, which is already about Egypt and is correct.

items.bewering: sfinks: 'n Beeld van 'n wese met 'n leeu se liggaam en gewoonlik 'n mens se kop.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Sphinx': Egyptian and Greek sphinxes are lion-bodied and typically human-headed; the ram-headed sphinxes (criosphinxes) of Thebes are why 'gewoonlik' is needed, and it is there.

items.bewering: tempel: 'n Gebou waar mense 'n god of gode vereer.
items.bron: Egypt Exploration Society, 'Temples in Ancient Egypt': a temple was a house for one or more deities. The general wording also holds outside Egypt, e.g. Hindu temples, as a stand-alone entry should.

items.bewering: kalksteen: 'n Soort rots wat mense uitkap om mee te bou en waarin water grotte kan uitvreet.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Solutional cave', and the US National Park Service, 'Karst Topography Model': weakly acidic rain and groundwater dissolve limestone and form caves, limestone being the most common host rock. Wikipedia, 'Great Pyramid of Giza': the core blocks are local quarried limestone, cased in Tura limestone. 'Uitvreet' is a fair plain word for dissolving.

items.bewering: vereer: Om aan 'n god of 'n persoon groot eer en respek te bewys.
items.bron: LangEek English-Dutch dictionary, 'revere': 'vereren', to honour or respect someone deeply (the Dutch cognate; no online Afrikaans dictionary entry could be reached, but the Afrikaans sense is the same and it covers both gods and people).

items.bewering: priester: Iemand wat in 'n tempel werk en die rituele vir die gode uitvoer.
items.bron: kaikki.org (Wiktionary data), Afrikaans 'priester': priest, a general religious term; Dutch dictionaries gloss it as 'geestelike, pastoor'. Read on its own, the entry defines the word, and the definition excludes the priests South African learners know: a Catholic or Anglican priest works in a church and serves one God, not 'die gode' in 'n tempel. It is true of ancient Egyptian priests (Egypt Exploration Society, 'Temples in Ancient Egypt') but false as a definition of the word.
items.regstelling: Either tie the entry to ancient Egypt, so it says that in ancient Egypt a priest was someone who worked in a temple and performed the rituals for the gods, or widen it to a general definition (someone who performs religious rituals and services for a faith) followed by the Egyptian case. Do not keep a general-looking definition that rules out a church priest.

items.bewering: ritueel: 'n Vaste reeks handelinge wat mense elke keer op dieselfde manier doen, dikwels vir 'n god.
items.bron: Wiktionary, 'ritual': a rite, or a repeated set of actions, often in a religious context. 'Dikwels vir 'n god' correctly leaves room for non-religious rituals.

items.bewering: erfenis: Dinge en gewoontes wat ons uit die verlede ontvang, bewaar en aan die volgende geslagte oordra.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, 'About us' (whc.unesco.org/en/about-us/): 'Heritage is our legacy from the past, what we live with today, and what we pass on to future generations.'

opsomming: Every claim in the six study blocks is true and sourced, including the age of the Great Pyramid, the Afrikaans names Chafra and Menkaoere, and the carefully hedged 'moontlik 'n beskermer' for the Sphinx, but two glossary entries, piramide and priester, are true only of ancient Egypt and false when read on their own (a pyramid is first a shape learners meet in Grade 5 Maths, and a church priest is a priest), so each needs tying to ancient Egypt or widening; the lesson makes no superlative claims and its one comparison, the temple as a house for the gods, maps correctly.
